target.statement: LoRA+IADA improves the average reasoning score (R-Avg) from 52.2 to 61.7 (+9.5) over LoRA-only on Qwen3-VL-2B.
target.table_ref: Table 1, rows B (LoRA-only) and D (IADA+LoRA), R-Avg and Δ(D−B)
target.dataset: Qwen3-VL-2B fine-tuned on LLaVA-Instruct-Mix (259K samples), evaluated on 11 benchmarks: MMMU, MathVista, ScienceQA, MMStar, AI2D, MME, POPE, RealWorldQA, ChartQA, TextVQA, OCRBench

compute.basis: The target requires fine-tuning a 2B VLM on 259K visual-instruction samples for 16,198 steps plus evaluating 11 VLM benchmarks; the paper used a single H200 GPU and reports no code, so an AI agent would have to implement IADA and run a full SFT/eval protocol, which is infeasible on an 8-core CPU-only 16GB laptop in hours.

blockers: No code or repository link in the paper; IADA and the exact training/eval pipeline would need to be reimplemented from scratch.
Target requires full supervised fine-tuning of Qwen3-VL-2B on 259K LLaVA-Instruct-Mix samples (16,198 optimization steps), not a small classic ML run.
Paper used a single NVIDIA H200 GPU; CPU-only training/inference on the target laptop is practically infeasible.
Evaluation requires running 11 vision-language benchmarks, many with large image sets and generation-based scoring.
Even the cheapest single-benchmark variant still requires the same full fine-tuning run, so the cost is dominated by SFT.
title: Mitigating the Reasoning Tax in Vision-Language Fine-Tuning with Input-Adaptive Depth Aggregation
